brief: J.P. Morgan's morning briefing reports geopolitics driving risk assets. Brent tested $110 overnight on Iran resuming ballistic missile production and Houthis nearing Bab al-Mandeb, then pared gains on reports Iran and Gulf states meet Monday to push a Hormuz deal, with oil, global yields and vol extending higher and APAC catching down while US and EA futures traded green. A hawkish ECB no-brainer hike added to the rates selloff, so a near-full October hike is now priced, about 90bps of tightening over the next year, while Econ keeps a December call. US headline PPI rose 0.4%m/m and core 0.2%, giving an early core PCE estimate of 0.20%m/m. Copper sold off as US tariffs looked less certain, though consensus 2027 earnings already discount about $12,000/t. Hedge funds re-grossed by 1.3z, the most since late June, but nets stayed at the 40th percentile and sentiment turned less constructive. The desk is tactically cautious on global equities, long US and Asia over EU, hedged on momentum, and bullish EM while expecting country and sector divergence.
